title: KeyProbe — keyboard tester for Windows, Linux, macOS and the web
description: KeyProbe lights up every key you press on an on-screen keyboard and shows the codes your system sent for it. Chatter and stuck-key detection. Free and open source.
pitch: Lights up every key you press on an on-screen keyboard and shows the codes your system sent for it.
f_keyboard_body: Untested keys stay plain, tested keys turn green, a held key turns amber, a stuck one red. Five layouts: ANSI 104, ISO 105, TKL 87, 75 % and 60 %.
f_codes_body: W3C code, Windows virtual-key code and name, PS/2 scan code with the extended flag, the raw scan code your system sent, and the USB HID usage. 138 keys, from public specifications.
f_chatter_body: A key that fires again less than 30 ms after its release gets a red mark; a key held longer than 5 seconds turns red. The event log shows the milliseconds between events.
f_themes_body: Three themes, undo for every reset and view change, and a list of the keys your system keeps for itself, so a missing key isn't blamed on the keyboard.
shot_main_alt: KeyProbe mid-test on the ANSI layout: tested keys in green, Shift held in amber, a chatter warning on F
shot_iso_alt: The light theme on the ISO 105 layout
shot_hc_alt: The high contrast theme on the 60 % layout
unsigned_note: The files aren't signed with a paid certificate. Windows SmartScreen: More info → Run anyway. macOS: right-click → Open the first time.
footer_license: Free and open source, MIT or Apache-2.0.
